Subject: Finova: Performance SLOs, regional routing & data residency — follow-up

Hi Aisha / Matt — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment going into procurement/arch review.

Call recap (high level)
- Primary use case: customer-facing conversational workflows with streaming responses for long-form guidance.
- Expected steady-state throughput: ~200 requests/sec, with traffic spikes up to ~500rps during peak business hours.
- Concurrency: typical per-customer concurrency ~4 sessions, but burst concurrency can hit 12 for some accounts.
- Latency SLO targets (per-region): US: p50 <= 40ms, p95 <= 140ms; EU: p50 <= 50ms, p95 <= 160ms; APAC: p50 <= 70ms, p95 <= 220ms.
- Streaming requirements: server-sent events / chunked streaming for progressive tokens, 50-60 token/sec sustain for large responses.
- Data residency: APAC customer data must remain in APAC; EU data must be processed/stored in EU per regs.

Attachments: redwood-slo-summary.pdf (summary of latency/throughput assumptions and recommended capacity profiles).

Open questions / next steps
1) Can you confirm the target regions (US, EU, APAC) and which customer segments require APAC-only data residency?
2) Procurement timing: are we aiming to get terms signed by EOY or early January?
3) For streaming, do you have an SLA requirement around first-token latency vs per-token throughput?

Proposed actions from Redwood
- We'll validate capacity sizing for 200rps steady with the concurrency profile and provide a Dedicated vs Hosted cost comparison. (Aditya to validate GPU pool sizing)
- Confirm that our regional routing can be configured per-tenant with enforced data residency and a private APAC deployment option for regulated customers. (Technical follow-up & architecture doc)
- Schedule a 60-min deep-dive next week to walk the Finova infra/security team through network/firewall, KMS options, and rollout plan.

If the above looks right, I’ll ask Aditya to send a short architecture note + proposed canary rollout and we can lock a time for the deep-dive.

Thanks — Marissa

Thanks Marissa — useful recap. Quick answers from our side:
- Regions: Yes — US and EU for our global customers; APAC is required for our APAC-retail line (about ~20% of traffic, primarily Australia & Singapore).
- Data residency: APAC-retail must keep PII and session transcripts in APAC. EU customers require EU-only processing for regulated accounts.
- SLA ask: first-token p95 ideally <= 200ms globally; then per-token streaming sustain at ~40-60 tokens/sec.
- Procurement: aiming for signed terms by Jan 10; reviewers include procurement and security.

Two additional questions:
1) For APAC data residency, do you support a hosted regional deployment (Redwood-managed in APAC) with contractual residency guarantees, or do we need a Private (customer-managed) deployment?
2) For encryption: we need to know if Redwood supports customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for all regions.

Thanks — quick technical answers and next steps.

Feasibility notes:
- Capacity: supporting 200rps steady with 500rps peaks is feasible. For streaming-heavy workloads we recommend a regional Dedicated pool for APAC (N GPU nodes, estimate 6x A100-style equivalent) to meet p95 targets. Hosted multi-region routing (Redwood-managed) can meet US/EU SLOs with regional clusters and smart routing.
- Latency: predicted p95 numbers look achievable with regional clusters and connection warm-up. APAC p95 at ~200ms is feasible with a dedicated APAC pool + edge routing.
- Data residency: We can provide a Redwood-managed hosted APAC deployment with contractual residency guarantees (data processed and stored in APAC region) for standard customers. For customers needing the highest compliance posture (strict audits/KMS in-customer control), we recommend Private deployment (customer-managed) in APAC.
- KMS: we support customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) across Hosted and Dedicated offerings; for Private deployments we support HSM integrations. Rishi, please add any additional compliance notes.
- Cross-region cache: session KV cache replication across regions can cause residency leakage if not careful. Recommended approach: per-tenant routing + per-region KV caches with optional encrypted replication only when allowed.

Attachments: network-topology.png (image/png, 420KB)
Next steps:
1) I’ll draft a short architecture note that outlines two options: (A) Hosted multi-region with contractual residency + per-tenant routing and (B) Dedicated/Private APAC pool for regulated customers. Expect that note by EOD Monday.
2) Schedule the Tue deep-dive — Marissa, can you confirm Finova’s preferred time?
3) If they want contractual residency in hosted APAC, Legal will need to review the data processing addendum; I’ll loop in Legal once Finova confirms.
